# SEO-COPD vs non_COPD

I want to find DMS specific for SEO-COPD. In order to do that I have to remove from this comparison the effect of common COPDs (cCOPD) and the effect of smoking. In the case of cCOPD vs controls (CS and ES) we can use the DMs obtained to remove from SEO_COPD. For the effect of smoking is done by comparing controls current smokers (CS) vs ex-smokers (ES).

```{r}
pheno.data = pheno.data2 %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    (Group_detailed == "control es" | Group_simple == "SEO-COPD")
    ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
   SEO_COPD_Y_or_N = as.factor(
      dplyr::case_when(
      SEO_COPD_Y_or_N == "Control" ~ "Control_ES",
      TRUE ~ SEO_COPD_Y_or_N
     )
    ) 
  )%>%
  readr::write_csv(
    .,
    paste0(results.dir,"pheno.data_SEOvsCtrl_ES.csv")
    )
pheno.data
```

```{r}
boxplot.color.group <- function(pheno.data, m.value){
      groups <- as.factor(pheno.data$SEO_COPD_Y_or_N)
      # Assign a unique color to each group level
      # Sort the data by groups to ensure grouping
      sorted.indices <- order(groups)  # Get the order of the samples by group

      groups <- groups[sorted.indices]  # Rearrange the grouping factor
      
      group.colors <- rainbow(length(levels(groups)))  # Or use custom colors
      names(group.colors) <- levels(groups) 
      # Create the boxplot with grouping

              main = "M-value distribution across samples",
              col = group.colors[groups],
              xlab = "Samples grouped by levels",
              las = 2)  # Rotate axis labels for readability
      
      # Add group separation lines (optional)
      abline(v = cumsum(table(groups)) + 0.5, col = "blue",  lty = 3, lwd = 3)
}
```

# Filter and keep biologically relevant


```{r}
mtx.win.betas <- as.matrix(ENmix::M2B(mtx.m.values))

# Match samples in the beta matrix with metadata
ctrl.samples <- pheno.data[pheno.data$SEO_COPD_Y_or_N == "Control_ES",]  # Samples in the control group
seo.COPD.samples <- pheno.data[pheno.data$SEO_COPD_Y_or_N == "SEO_COPD",] # Samples in the disease group

ctrl.betas <- mtx.win.betas[, colnames(mtx.win.betas) %in% rownames(ctrl.samples)]
copd.betas <- mtx.win.betas[, colnames(mtx.win.betas) %in% rownames(seo.COPD.samples)]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Calculate mean methylation levels for each CpG
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate mean beta values for each CpG (row)
ctrl.means <- rowMeans(ctrl.betas, na.rm = TRUE)
copd.means <- rowMeans(copd.betas, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a dataframe with one CpG per row
cpgs.df <- data.frame(
  CpG = rownames(mtx.win.betas),
  ctrl_mean = ctrl.means,
  SEO_mean = copd.means,
  delta_mean = copd.means - ctrl.means
)

# Add absolute delta mean
cpgs.df$abs_delta_mean <- abs(cpgs.df$delta_mean)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Apply final filters
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Define filtering criteria
MIN_DELTA <- 0.05      # 5% minimum methylation difference
MIN_BETA <- 0.2         # Lower bound for mean beta value
MAX_BETA <- 0.8         # Upper bound for mean beta value

# Apply filters:
# 1. Absolute methylation difference > 5%
# 2. Mean beta values between 20-80% in both groups
filtered.cpgs <- cpgs.df[
  cpgs.df$abs_delta_mean > MIN_DELTA &
  cpgs.df$SEO_mean > MIN_BETA & cpgs.df$SEO_mean < MAX_BETA &
  cpgs.df$ctrl_mean > MIN_BETA & cpgs.df$ctrl_mean < MAX_BETA,
]

# View the filtered results
head(filtered.cpgs)

idx.cpgs <- match(rownames(filtered.cpgs), base::rownames(m.values))
mtx.m.values <- m.values[idx.cpgs,]
dim(mtx.m.values)
```
# Winsorization per sample

```{r}
# Function to apply winsorization on EPIC array data
winsorize.epic.array <- function(data) {
  # Ensure the data is in a data frame format
  data <- as.data.frame(data)
  
  # Apply winsorization per sample (column-wise)
  winsorized.data <- data %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ {
      # Calculate Q1, Q3, and IQR for the column (CpG-specific)
      Q1 <- quantile(., 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
      Q3 <- quantile(., 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
      IQR <- Q3 - Q1
      
      # Define thresholds for extreme values (EVs)
      lower.threshold <- Q1 - (1.5 * IQR) # I use 1.5 times from IQR, more stringent.
      upper.threshold <- Q3 + (1.5 * IQR)
      
      # Winsorize values: replace EVs with thresholds
      . <- ifelse(. < lower.threshold, lower.threshold, .)
      . <- ifelse(. > upper.threshold, upper.threshold, .)
      
      return(.)
    }))
  
  return(winsorized.data)
}
```

```{r}
# Apply winsorization
win.samples.m.values <- winsorize.epic.array(mtx.m.values)
boxplot.color.group(pheno.data = pheno.data, m.value = win.samples.m.values)
```

# Truncate m values in +-5 mvalues
I truncate the m-values because m values around +-16 indicate 0 or 1 beta values, which are biological irrelevant. This extreme values can be due to batch effect most likely, in principle these extreme values could be cause by biology but I have no way to verify this with the data I have.
This approach is not correct here, because of the very low number of samples and high variance I have a lot of extreme values, this produce two picks in the distribution of m values around the trimmed cut-off.

# Run the regression model
One problem I have is that because the low number of samples and high variance the addition of control PCs to my model produce a drastic reduction of the degrees of freedom. What I try to do then is to run i.e Combat to correct batch effect and avoid adding more parameters to my model. Also not working with Combat, two few samples per batch, the algo cannot generalize. 

+ PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + PC6 + PC7

```{r}
sample_keep =  which(rownames(pheno.data) %in% base::colnames(win.samples.m.values))
pheno.data = pheno.data[sample_keep,]

idx.subjects <- match(rownames(pheno.data), base::colnames(win.samples.m.values))
m.values <- win.samples.m.values[,idx.subjects]
dim(m.values)

```

```{r warning=FALSE, message=True, eval=FALSE}
start.time <- Sys.time()

design <- model.matrix(
  ~0 + SEO_COPD_Y_or_N + Age + Gender + PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + PC6 + PC7 ,
  data = pheno.data 
  )

original.fit <- limma::lmFit(
  m.values,
  design,
  na.exclude=TRUE,
  method = "robust",
  maxit = 1000
)

elapsed.time <- Sys.time() - start.time
print(elapsed.time)
```


```{r}
file.orig.fit <- file.path(results.dir, "limma_original_fit_age_gender_PC1_7_filtered_mean.RDS")
saveRDS(original.fit, 
        file = file.orig.fit)

#ori.fit <- readRDS(
#  file.orig.fit
#  )
```


```{r warning=FALSE, message=True, eval=FALSE}
# create a contrast matrix for specific comparisons
cont.matrix <- limma::makeContrasts(
  test = SEO_COPD_Y_or_NSEO_COPD - SEO_COPD_Y_or_NControl_ES, 
  levels = design
)

# Fit the contrasts
adjusted.fit <- limma::contrasts.fit(original.fit, cont.matrix)

# Calculate the moderate t-statistics that uses pooling
# Use empirical Bayes (eBayes) for small sample sizes.
adjusted.fit <- limma::eBayes(
                      fit = adjusted.fit,
                      robust = TRUE,
                      )

```

## Estimate Inflation
Genomic inflation factor
zscore = (x-μ)/σ

```{r}
effect.size = adjusted.fit$coefficients
stdError = sqrt(adjusted.fit$s2.post) * adjusted.fit$stdev.unscaled

zvalue <- effect.size / stdError
chisq  <- (zvalue) ^ 2

lambda_infl <- median(
  chisq,
  ) / qchisq(p = 0.5, df =  1)

print(paste0("lamda using effect size and SE: ", round(lambda_infl, 3)))
```

```{r}
all_p_values <- results$P.Value
# Sort p-values in ascending order
sorted_p_values <- sort(all_p_values)
```

```{r}
explore_regression_results <- function(DMPs){
  # ---ANALYZE THE EFFECT SIZE DISTRIBUTION ---
  # Calculate the absolute log fold changes for every CpG
  all_abs_logFC <- abs(DMPs$logFC)

  # Generate percentiles to understand the distribution
  effect_size_percentiles <- quantile(
    all_abs_logFC,
    probs = c(0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 1.0),
    na.rm = TRUE
    )
  print("Distribution of Absolute M-value LogFC:")
  print(effect_size_percentiles)
  
  # Let's choose a threshold that represents the top 1% of effect sizes.
  # This is a stringent and biologically justified choice.
  logFC_threshold <- effect_size_percentiles["99%"]
  print(paste("Chosen effect size threshold (99th percentile):", round(logFC_threshold, 3)))
  
  # Explore the data
  print(paste0("Total significant probes: ", dim(DMPs[DMPs$adj.P.Val < 0.05,])[1])) 
  # 0 < LogFC
  print(
    paste0(
      "Significant probes with positive LogFC: ",
      dim(DMPs[DMPs$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & DMPs$logFC > logFC_threshold,])[1]
      )
    )
  # 0> LogFC
  print(paste0(
    "Significant probes with negative logFC: ",
    dim(DMPs[DMPs$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & DMPs$logFC < -logFC_threshold,])[1]
    )
  ) 
  DMPs.filtered <- subset(DMPs, 
                        adj.P.Val < 0.05 & 
                        abs(logFC) > logFC_threshold)
  print(paste0(
    "final filetered robust DMPS:  ",
     length(unique(DMPs.filtered$CpG.id))
   )
  )
  return(DMPs.filtered)
}
dmps.filter <- explore_regression_results(results)
dmps.filter
```

### Power analysis paper:
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31088362/

"The recommended significance threshold for DNA methylation association analyses is P < 9.42x10-8 as determined from a permutation analysis."

```{r}
# genome-wide sig cpgs
sig <- ifelse(DMPs$`P.Value` < 9e-8, 1, 0)
table(sig)  # 1 sig
```
